implemented_requirements.evidence: constants.BOARD_SIZE is set to 3 and gui.py creates a 3x3 matrix of tk.Buttons using BOARD_SIZE.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Two players alternate turns (X and O)
implemented_requirements.evidence: gui.TicTacToeGUI stores current_player, initialized to PLAYER_X, and toggles it after each valid move.
game_logic.Board records every move in self.move_history and provides get_move_history().

implemented_requirements.requirement: Players place X or O symbols
implemented_requirements.evidence: When a move is made, Board stores PLAYER_X or PLAYER_O; _render_move() displays the symbol with appropriate color.
Board.check_winner() iterates over all possible lines (rows, columns, diagonals) and returns the winner and winning line.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect a draw when board is full
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_full() checks for any EMPTY cells; gui._on_cell_click() calls _end_game() with a draw message when is_full() is true and no winner.

implemented_requirements.requirement: End the game when a win or draw occurs
implemented_requirements.evidence: gui._end_game() sets self.game_over = True, updates scores, highlights winning cells, and prevents further clicks.
gui.py builds a Tkinter window with title, status label, colored buttons, hover effects, a reset button, and a scoreboard.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ability to start a new game
implemented_requirements.evidence: Reset button calls _reset_game(), which clears the board, resets state, and updates UI.

judge.summary: The submitted files provide a complete, functional tic‑tac‑toe implementation. Constants define a 3×3 board, game_logic implements move validation, win/draw detection, and move history, while gui.py offers a Tkinter UI with turn tracking, visual feedback, score keeping, and a reset feature. All core requirements are satisfied and the code appears ready to run, yielding a pass.
